draws.name: Controlled hunts drawing — elk, pronghorn, deer (incl. youth and motor-vehicle/non-ambulatory deer)
Landowner antelope drawing (owners/operators of 160+ acres in Cimarron or Texas County)
draws.quote: 2026 Landowner Antelope Application Period: March 9 – March 30 Results will be released in early April

pointOnly.name: Preference Point Only (PPO), chosen per category inside the controlled-hunt application
pointOnly.quote: This option will only be available during the online Controlled Hunt application period.

fees.label: Controlled hunts application fee (once per person per year, all categories)
fees.notes: Paid once per person per year regardless of categories entered. Covers up to 14 hunt choices across four categories.
fees.quote: must pay an application fee ($10 for residents; $50 for nonresidents) to enter the Controlled Hunts drawing

fees.label: Controlled hunts application fee — nonresident
fees.notes: CONFLICT: the Cost page says $50 for nonresidents, but the hub, Need-to-Know and Step-by-Step pages say a flat '$10 application fee' with no residency split. Confirm with ODWC before showing.
fees.quote: must pay an application fee ($10 for residents; $50 for nonresidents) to enter the Controlled Hunts drawing

fees.label: Extra preference point (one per category per year) — resident
fees.notes: Optional add-on that adds one more point on top of the point earned for not being drawn. Separate from Preference Point Only, which is covered by the standard application fee.
fees.quote: one additional preference point in all hunt categories at a cost of $10 for residents and $50 for nonresidents

fees.label: Extra preference point (one per category per year) — nonresident
fees.quote: one additional preference point in all hunt categories at a cost of $10 for residents and $50 for nonresidents

fees.label: PointGuard insurance — resident
fees.notes: Optional; protects points if you draw but cannot attend.
fees.quote: PointGuard insurance is available for an additional $10 for residents or $50 for nonresidents.

fees.label: PointGuard insurance — nonresident
fees.quote: PointGuard insurance is available for an additional $10 for residents or $50 for nonresidents.

fees.label: Extra hunt choice beyond the standard limit
fees.quote: Applicants may also add extra hunt choices beyond the standard limit for $3 each.

fees.label: Resident elk license (charged only if drawn)
fees.notes: Resident annual/fiscal-year license holders; lifetime and youth (under 18) license holders pay no license fee per the Cost table.
fees.quote: Elk Residents age 18 or older (required for each elk hunted) | $51

fees.label: Resident antelope license (charged only if drawn)
fees.quote: Antelope Residents age 18 or older (required for each antelope hunted) | $51

fees.label: Resident bonus deer license for a controlled deer hunt (charged only if drawn)
fees.notes: From the Cost page table 'Bonus Deer License' column, resident annual/fiscal-year row.

fees.label: Nonresident controlled-hunt permit fee (charged only if drawn)
fees.notes: Charged in addition to the nonresident species license.

fees.label: Nonresident elk license
fees.quote: Nonresident Elk Nonresidents age 18 or older (required for each elk hunted) | $506

fees.label: Nonresident antelope license
fees.quote: Nonresident Antelope Nonresidents age 18 or older (required for each antelope hunted) | $506

fees.label: Nonresident deer license (controlled hunt)
fees.notes: Nonresidents do not need to buy the deer license before applying; it is charged if drawn.

fees.label: Federal user fee — Wichita Mountains NWR elk hunt
fees.notes: Federal areas charge their own fees (deer hunts on federal areas mostly $20; McAlester AAP $40).

fees.label: Resident annual hunting license (age 18+)
fees.notes: Other qualifying licenses: annual combination ($53), 3-year combination, lifetime. Residents under 16 are exempt.
fees.quote: Annual Hunting Residents age 18 or older | $36 | 365 Days

fees.label: Nonresident annual hunting license (age 18+)
fees.notes: Nonresident youth annual super hunting license is $151. Need-to-Know lists the nonresident 5-day license as qualifying to apply, but the fee page says the 5-day license is not valid for big game.
fees.quote: Nonresident Annual Hunting Nonresidents age 18 or older | $209 | 365 Days

prerequisites.text: Hold a valid Oklahoma hunting license for the current calendar year before you apply (residents under 16 exempt). The license is nonrefundable if you do not draw.
prerequisites.quote: All applicants (residents and non-residents) must possess or purchase a valid Oklahoma hunting license for the current calendar year of the drawing.

prerequisites.text: Apprentice-license holders may apply for elk and pronghorn, but must be hunter-education certified before the hunt.
prerequisites.quote: they must be hunter education-certified prior to participating in those controlled hunts

prerequisites.text: Elk and pronghorn controlled hunts are once in a lifetime; once drawn you can never apply in that category again.
prerequisites.quote: Since elk and antelope hunts are once-in-a-lifetime hunts, successful applicants are never again eligible to apply for those categories.

prerequisites.text: Apply online only; you need a credit/debit card. Drawn applicants are charged permit and federal fees automatically.
prerequisites.quote: successful applicants will be automatically charged for any required permit or federal fees required for the hunt they've been awarded
